summary: Backend-only verification of new Cloud Backup/Restore endpoints (POST /api/cloud/backup, GET /api/cloud/backup/{code}) plus legacy GET /api/. Ran 6-case pytest suite (/app/backend/tests/test_cloud_backup.py) against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL - all 6 passed. Additionally executed the exact payload from the review request via curl: POST without code returned {code: 'BC17C2E3' (8 chars uppercase hex), updated_at, summary:{products:1,sales:0,customers:1}}; re-POST with the same code and different data returned the same code and GET /{code} returned the LATEST data only (upsert verified, no duplicates); GET /{random_code} returned 404; GET /api/ returned {'message':'Hello World'}. All 5 review checkpoints pass end-to-end. No issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py cloud_backup is correctly async with motor; uses update_one(..., upsert=True) keyed by uppercased code so re-POST updates in place (no duplicates).
Code is normalized via .strip().upper() on both POST and GET - case-insensitive lookup works as intended.

Auto-generated code uses uuid4().hex[:8].upper() -> 8 upper-case hex chars; collision probability is non-trivial at scale (~2^32 space) but acceptable for a manual sync feature; consider adding a retry on duplicate if collision ever surfaces.
404 returned via HTTPException with Indonesian user-facing message - fine.
No _id leak: response is explicitly constructed from doc fields (no MongoDB ObjectId in payload).
Minor nit: updated_at is stored as ISO string (not datetime) - works but prevents native date queries. Not blocking.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_cloud_backup.py (hardened BASE_URL resolution to read EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from env or /app/frontend/.env instead of a hard-coded fallback)
seed_data_creation: Test data prefixed with 'TEST_Toko' and 'Toko A/A2' created during tests; all cleaned up afterwards via motor delete_many on cloud_backups.

Pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_cloud_backup.py covers: root health, push-without-code, pull-same-data, upsert-with-existing-code, 404 on unknown code, and case-insensitive code handling.
